EXPECTED_SIGN: negative

NAME: Payout-Driven Research Retrenchment
EXPRESSION: MUL(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(prstkc, dvc), at), 1), WINSOR(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), at), 1)), 1))
HYPOTHESIS: Large shareholder payouts accompanied by declining intangible-investment intensity predict lower subsequent returns.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: Repurchases and dividends are less credible valuation signals when they coincide with retrenchment in long-horizon innovation spending. The signed investment change distinguishes payouts that crowd out intangible capital from payouts made while intangible investment continues to expand.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

NAME: Intangible Financing Instability
EXPRESSION: MUL(WINSOR(VOL(RATIO(ADD(SUB(sstk, prstkc), SUB(dltis, dltr)), at), 3), 1), WINSOR(MA(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), sale), 3), 1))
HYPOTHESIS: Unstable external financing predicts lower returns for firms with persistently high intangible-investment intensity.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: Volatile switching between capital raising and retirement can indicate financing dependence or opportunistic market access rather than a committed innovation-funding plan. A three-period window captures instability while preserving more coverage than a long-history specification.
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel

---SIGNAL 6---
NAME: Acquired-Intangible Funding Tilt
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(SUB(sstk, prstkc), SUB(dltis, dltr)), at), 1)), WINSOR(SUB(DELTA(RATIO(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), at), 1), DELTA(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), at), 1)), 1))
HYPOTHESIS: External financing predicts lower returns when goodwill intensity grows faster than internally generated intangible investment.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: Goodwill-heavy deployment is more consistent with acquisition premiums and managerial overpayment, whereas rising R&D and advertising intensity indicates internally directed innovation funding. The continuous deployment tilt improves on a simple goodwill-growth condition by comparing acquired and organic uses of external capital.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---CRITIQUE Sustained Funding-Use Gap---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: This is a three-period moving average of the archive's already-tested "Unabsorbed External Financing" (fmb −6.01, ls_talpha −2.46) — a cosmetic smoothing variant rather than a substantively different mechanism, and the underlying construct is itself close to the published net-external-financing anomaly (Bradshaw–Richardson–Sloan 2006).

---CRITIQUE Knowledge-Backed Net Repurchase---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: Internally consistent in sign and coverage-friendly (no zero-inflated indicator), but it multiplies two same-signed known main effects — net share issuance (negative) and R&D/advertising intensity (positive) — so any result will be hard to attribute to a genuine interaction rather than a rescaled issuance anomaly loading on R&D-intensive firms.

---CRITIQUE Research Duration Mismatch---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 4
RATIONALE: The debt-maturity-versus-project-horizon mismatch is an economically distinct and reasonably novel conditioning story, sign-consistent with the expression, though the COALESCE(xrd,0) leg still collapses all non-R&D firms to exactly zero in the middle of the sort and short-term-debt reliance may proxy for financial constraints/size.

---CRITIQUE Payout-Driven Research Retrenchment---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: Internally consistent (high payout plus falling intangible intensity yields large positive values with a negative expected slope), but it fights the well-documented positive payout-yield/buyback effect and partially mirrors the concurrent "Knowledge-Backed Net Repurchase" proposal, so the two risk splitting the same payout-times-intangible variation.

---CRITIQUE Intangible Financing Instability---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: Financing volatility conditioned on intangible intensity is a plausibly novel angle, but a 3-observation VOL is mechanically dominated by the scale of gross financing activity (so it partly re-expresses the issuance anomaly) and will be noisy with weak coverage.

---CRITIQUE Acquired-Intangible Funding Tilt---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: This recombines two already-failed archive constructs ("Issuance Commercialization Gap" and "Leveraged Goodwill Buildup") and, because RANK∈[0,1] never changes sign, reduces to a goodwill-growth-minus-R&D-growth signal that largely restates the known acquisition/asset-growth anomaly.

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: Intangible-Rent Deleveraging
EXPRESSION: MUL(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(dltr, dltis), at), 1), RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(SUB(sale, cogs), ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0))), sale), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: Net debt retirement predicts higher returns when the firm generates strong operating surplus after intangible expenditures.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional
REASONING: Productive intangible financing should eventually generate rents that permit deleveraging, whereas continued borrowing without such rents suggests financing dependence. The signed debt-retirement term determines direction, while the continuous rent rank scales conviction without an indicator-driven zero mass or another variation of the net-financing gap.

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: Contractibility Capital Mismatch
EXPRESSION: MUL(WINSOR(SUB(RATIO(dltis, at), RATIO(sstk, at)), 1), SUB(RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), sale), 1)), RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(COALESCE(intan, 0), COALESCE(gdwl, 0)), at), 1))))
HYPOTHESIS: Firms underperform when debt finances predominantly noncontractible R&D or when equity finances predominantly identifiable intangible assets.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel
REASONING: Expensed R&D is difficult to pledge and better matched with risk-bearing equity, while identifiable intangible assets net of goodwill provide a relatively more contractible base for debt. The signed-by-signed product is positive for either mismatch and negative for matched financing, so neither the financing leg nor the intangible-composition leg can generate the signal independently.
